ἴσως ὁ τοιοῦτος ἐρεῖ ὡς τὰ αὐτὰ ὀνόματα τίθησι διττῶς ἡ γραφή, ποτὲ μὲν ἐπὶ τῶν
σωματικῶν, ὅτε δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ πνευματικοῦ· ὡς καὶ περὶ τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος γεγραμμένον,
ἐν ᾧ τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸ πιεῖν κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον ὅτε μὲν ἐπὶ τοῦ σωματικοῦ ὅτε δὲ
ἐπὶ τοῦ πνευματικοῦ τετάχθαι δοκεῖ· καὶ τὸ περὶ τοῦ θερι μοῦ ὡσαύτως φησίν. φήσει
τοίνυν οὐδὲν θαυμαστὸν κατὰ τοῦτον τὸν χαρακτῆρα καὶ τὸν ἀπόστολον εἰρηκέναι,
τὸ μὲν ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ τάσσοντα οὐκ ἐπὶ τοῦ κοινοτέρου θανάτου, τὸ δὲ
θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει, ὡς θανάτου νῦν τοῦ μέσου ὀνομαζομένου. ἕτερος δὲ
παρὰ τοῦτον ἐρεῖ ὅτι θάνατος ἐνταῦθα λέγεται ὁ κυριεύων Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἄλλος ἢ ὁ
ἐχθρὸς αὐτοῦ οὗ τύπος ἦν τὸ κατὰ τὸν Ἰωνᾶν κῆτο προφητευόμενον καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ
Ἰὼβ φάσκοντος ἀλλὰ καταρά αιτο αὐτὴν ὁ μέλλων τὸ μέγα κῆτο χειρώ α θαι. πρὸς
ὃν θάνατον ὁδεύων κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦ μέσου θανάτου ἔλεγεν, οὐ διὰ τὸν μέσον
θάνατον ἀλλὰ δι' ἐκεῖνον, νῦν ἡ ψυχή μου τετάρακται καὶ περίλυπό ἐ τιν ἡ ψυχή
μου ἕω θανάτου. οἱονεὶ γὰρ ἀπῄει εἰς τὴν χώραν αὐτοῦ διὰ τοὺς κρατουμένους ὑπ'
αὐτοῦ, ὡς τάχα διὰ τοῦτο εἰρῆσθαι τὸ εἰ χοῦν θανάτου κατήγαγέ με. καὶ ἑαυτὸν
πεποίηκεν αὐτῷ ὑποχείριον ὑπήκοο γενόμενο μέχρι θανάτου. διὰ γὰρ τὸ γεγονέναι
ἐν αὐτῷ κατακριθεὶς ὑπ' αὐτοῦ κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν οὖσαν ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ
θανάτῳ. ὡσάν τις παραδείγματος ἕνεκεν ἐλεύθερος ὢν δοῦλον ἑαυτὸν παραδίδωσιν
τῷ στρατηγῷ τῶν πολεμίων, ἵνα παρ' αὐτῷ γενόμενος ἐλευθερώσῃ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ
οἰκονομικῇ δουλείᾳ τοὺς πολίτας ἀπὸ τοῦ ὑπ' ἐκείνῳ κινδύνου, διὰ τοῦ ἐνέδρᾳ τινὶ
ἀποκτεῖναι τὸν στρατηγὸν καὶ τοὺς ὑπ' αὐτῷ πολεμίους· ἐκυριεύθη γὰρ ὁ τοῦτο
δράσας ὡς οὐκ αἰχμάλωτος ἁλοὺς ἀλλὰ φρονήματι χρησάμενος ἀριστέως. οὕτως οὖν
καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἑαυτὸν παρέδωκεν τῇ δουλείᾳ, ἵνα μηδεὶς θανάτου γένηται τῶν
μαθητευομένων αὐτοῦ τῷ λόγῳ δοῦλος· οὗτος γὰρ ὡς φησὶν ἡ γραφὴ κατήργη ε τὸν
τὸ κράτο ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου, τοῦτ' ἐ τὶν τὸν διάβολον, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. τάχα δὲ καὶ
παρέδωκεν ἑαυτὸν τῷ θανάτῳ κυριευθησόμενον ῥυόμενος τοὺς ὑπ' αὐτοῦ
κεκρατημένους καὶ ἀντ' ἐκείνων ἑαυτὸν προδιδούς, ἵνα μετὰ τοῦτο καταστρατηγήσῃ
καὶ καταργή ῃ τὸν θάνατον. 31 vi 12–14 μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ
ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ· μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ
μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ· ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ ὡς ἐκ
νεκρῶν ζῶντας, καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ θεῷ· ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ
κυριεύσει· οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλ' ὑπὸ χάριν. ἀνωτέρω μὲν εἶπεν ἵνα ὥ περ
ἐβα ίλευ εν ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ, νυνὶ δὲ οὐκ εἶπεν τοῦτο ἀλλὰ μὴ βασιλευέτω ἡ
ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι, διδάσκων ὅτι ὥσπερ θρόνος καὶ βασίλειόν ἐστι
τῆς ἁμαρτίας τὸ θνητὸν ἡμῶν σῶμα· τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆ αρκὸ ἔχθρα εἰ θεόν, καὶ
πάλιν τὸ φρόνημα τῆ αρκὸ θάνατο . ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντα τὰ ἁμαρτήματα ἔργα αρκό
ἐστιν ἅπερ ὁ ἀπόστολος φανερὰ ὠνόμασεν. ἐν αὐτοῖς δὲ τάξας καὶ τὰς αἱρέ ει
ἐδίδαξεν ὅτι καὶ αὗται αρκό εἰσιν ἔργον, ἀπολύων ἡμᾶς περισπασμοῦ, ἵνα μὴ νομί
ζωμεν τινὰ μὲν εἶναι ἔργα αρκό , τινὰ δὲ ἁμαρτήματα οὐ αρκὸ μὲν ἤτοι δὲ ψυχῆς ἢ
νοῦ. ἀλλ' ἐπάν τις ζητῇ πῶς καὶ αἱρέ ει ἐν τοῖς ἔργοι τῆ αρκό εἰσι κατειλεγμέναι,
λεκτέον πρὸς αὐτὸν ὅτι αἱρέ ει γίνονται ἀπὸ τοῦ νοῦ τῆ αρκό , περὶ οὗ φησί που ὁ
Παῦλος εἰκῆ ἐμβατεύων καὶ φυ ιούμενο ὑπὸ τοῦ νοὸ τῆ αρκὸ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐ
κρατῶν τὴν κεφαλήν. τάχα δὲ καὶ ὅτε ἁμαρτάνομεν βασιλευούσης τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐν
τῷ θνητῷ ἡμῶν σώματι οὐδὲν ἄλλο ἐσμὲν ἤπερ τὸ θνητὸν σῶμα καὶ άρκε · οὐ μὴ
γάρ φησι καταμείνῃ τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐν τοῖ ἀνθρώποι τούτοι εἰ τὸν αἰῶνα διὰ τὸ
εἶναι αὐτοὺ άρκα . καὶ αὐτὴ δὲ ἡ ψυχὴ ἔοικε μὴ μένειν, ἀλλ' ἤτοι διὰ κακίαν
γίνεσθαι σὰρξ ἢ δι' ἀρετὴν πνεῦμα· ὅτε γὰρ κολλᾶται τῇ πόρνῃ γίνεται εἰ άρκα μίαν
pass_a_gloss: Perhaps someone will say that the scripture uses the same names twice, sometimes regarding bodily things, sometimes regarding spiritual things, as it is written about the Samaritan woman, where water and drinking are placed in the same location sometimes for the bodily, sometimes for the spiritual, and likewise he speaks about the heat; thus it is not surprising according to this character and the apostle to have said that we died with Christ, being ordered not to the common death, but his death no longer rules, as death now called the middle; another will say that death spoken of here is the ruling death of Christ, no other than his enemy whose type was the whale prophesied about Jonah and spoken of by Job, yet he curses it, the one about to seize the great whale with hand; going toward that death according to the time of the middle death, he spoke, not because of the middle death but because of that one, now my soul is troubled and grievously pained, soul of mine toward death; for as if going into his land through those held by him, perhaps therefore it was said, 'I brought you down from the dust of death'; and he made himself subject to him, becoming obedient even to death; for having been condemned in him, he condemned the sin that was in that death; as a free person giving himself as a slave to the enemy commander, that having come to him he might free his own economic slavery of citizens from the danger from him, by ambush killing the commander and those under him; for the one doing this was ruled not as a captive taken but as one using wisdom excellently; thus also Christ gave himself to slavery, that none of his disciples taught by the word might become slaves of death; for as the scripture says, he abolished the one holding the power of death, that is the devil, and the following; and perhaps he gave himself to death, being about to be ruled, flowing to free those held under him and instead giving himself over, that afterward he might act as commander and abolish death; 31 vi 12–14: therefore let not sin reign in your mortal body to obey it in its lusts, nor present your members as instruments of injustice to sin, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God; for sin of yours will not rule; for you are not under law but under grace; above he said that just as sin reigned in death, now he does not say that but 'let not sin reign in your mortal body', teaching that just as a throne and kingdom is sin, so our mortal body is; for the mind of the flesh is enmity against God, and again the mind of the flesh is death; but also all sins are works of the flesh which the apostle openly named; among them he ordered and the choices he taught that these also are works of the flesh, freeing us from distraction, that we might not think some things are works of the flesh, others are sins not of the flesh but either of soul or mind; but if anyone seeks how choices are among the works of the flesh, let it be said to him that choices arise from the mind of the flesh, concerning which Paul says somewhere that he goes in empty and is puffed up under the mind of his flesh and does not hold his head; and perhaps when we sin while sin reigns in our mortal body, we are nothing other than our mortal body and flesh; for he does not say that my spirit remains in these people into the age because they are flesh; and this soul indeed seems not to remain, but either to become flesh through wickedness or spirit through virtue; for when it joins to the prostitute, it becomes flesh one;
pass_b_english: It might be objected that Scripture employs identical terms in dual senses—sometimes referring to physical realities, at other times to spiritual truths—just as the encounter with the Samaritan woman presents water and drinking in the same setting, now signifying bodily thirst, now the soul’s longing. Likewise, when heat is mentioned, the reference shifts according to context. Thus, it should not surprise us that the apostle declares we have died with Christ, not to the ordinary death shared by all, but to a death from which his dominion no longer extends—a death now termed the ‘middle’ death. Another interpreter may argue that the death in view here is the sovereign death that Christ overcame, none other than his adversary, whose foreshadowing appears in the great sea creature prophesied against Jonah and lamented by Job, which he nonetheless curses—the one destined to be seized by the hand of the coming deliverer. Moving toward that death in accordance with the season of the middle death, he spoke not because of that intermediate state, but because of the ultimate one: now my soul is shaken and deeply distressed, my soul drawing near to death. For as if entering his realm through those under his control, perhaps it was for this reason declared, ‘I brought you up from the dust of death.’ And he subjected himself to him, becoming obedient even unto death. Having been condemned in him, he condemned the sin residing in that death—just as a free person might enslave himself to the enemy commander, so that, by gaining access, he could liberate his people’s economic bondage from the threat posed by that foe, through ambush slaying the commander and his forces. For the one who acts thus is not regarded as a captive taken, but as one who employs wisdom with excellence. So too Christ gave himself into servitude, that none of his disciples, instructed by the word, might become enslaved to death. As Scripture affirms, he abolished the one who held the power of death, namely the devil, and what follows. Perhaps he also surrendered himself to death, about to be dominated, flowing to rescue those under his sway, and instead offering himself over, that afterward he might assume command and abolish death. [[Romans 6:12-14 >> Bible:Romans 6:12-14]]: Therefore, let sin not reign in your mortal body so as to obey its desires, nor offer your members as instruments of wickedness to sin; but present yourselves to God as those raised from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God. For sin will not have dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace. Earlier he said that just as sin once reigned in death, now he does not repeat that, but says, ‘Let sin not reign in your mortal body,’ teaching that just as a throne and kingdom belong to sin, so our mortal body is its domain. For the mind set on the flesh is hostility toward God, and again, the mind set on the flesh is death. Moreover, all sins are works of the flesh, which the apostle has explicitly named. Among them, he has enumerated and taught the choices, that these too are works of the flesh, to free us from distraction, so that we do not imagine some things are works of the flesh while others are sins not of the flesh but either of soul or mind. But if anyone inquires how these choices belong among the works of the flesh, let it be said that they arise from the mind of the flesh, concerning which Paul states somewhere that he enters empty and is inflated under the mind of his flesh, yet does not lift up his head. And perhaps, when we sin while sin reigns in our mortal body, we are nothing other than that mortal body and flesh; for he does not say that my spirit remains in these people into the age because they are flesh. And this soul indeed seems not to endure, but either to become flesh through wickedness or spirit through virtue. For when it unites with the prostitute, it becomes flesh—a single entity.

choices.issue: The nature of the 'middle death' referenced in the gloss
choices.choice: It refers to a transitional state between physical and spiritual death, distinct from both the common death of humanity and the ultimate defeat of death by Christ.

choices.issue: The relationship between sin, the flesh, and the mind in Pauline anthropology
choices.choice: Sin reigns through the mind set on the flesh, which is equated with death and hostility toward God, making all sins works of the flesh, including erroneous choices that arise from this corrupted mindset.
